opportunities.title: PHP2Shell: The Bug That Ate the Internet Before Anyone Patched It — AWS Confirms Attacks Predate Disclosure
opportunities.why_now: Exploitation is active at mass scale right now (UK gov outages, Mirai payloads, millions of attempts) making this the week's defining incident, not just another CVE.
opportunities.angle: Running incident timeline/digest: disclosure date vs. first observed exploitation, who's been hit (UK gov, AWS customers), and why patch cadence failed everyone simultaneously.

opportunities.title: Microsoft Says Chinese Spies Walked Into 2,250 Cloud Tenants Through ConnectWise — Meet the AI Pentest Tool That Got Them In
opportunities.why_now: Fresh attribution (Storm-0940) plus a novel detail — attackers using an AI pentesting tool called Artex — makes this the standout nation-state story of the week.
opportunities.angle: Breach anatomy post: how a single MSP tool compromise cascaded into thousands of tenant breaches, with the AI-tooling angle as the hook.

opportunities.title: The CA That Couldn't: eMudhra's 'Laughably Weak' Private Keys and the Slow Death of a Certificate Authority
opportunities.why_now: eMudhra's exit from the SSL/TLS business after guessable intermediate CA keys is a rare, concrete collapse of trust infrastructure worth dissecting while it's fresh.
opportunities.angle: Explainer/autopsy: what 'guessable' CA keys actually means, how this echoes past CA failures (DigiNotar comparison), and what it means for sites that trusted those certs.

opportunities.title: Third Time's Not the Charm: VeloCloud Zero-Day #3 in Four Months Shows Patch Cadence Is Broken
opportunities.why_now: A third zero-day in the same product within four months is a pattern story that practically writes the 'inevitable breach' thesis for you.
opportunities.angle: Trend piece: timeline of all three VeloCloud zero-days, what Arista/VMware got wrong each time, and whether 'patch and pray' SD-WAN security is sustainable.

opportunities.title: LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack Is Quietly Hoovering Up AI Infra Credentials — And Nobody's Watching the AI Stack
opportunities.why_now: Back-to-back LiteLLM coverage from Register and SecurityWeek signals a real, spreading supply-chain compromise hitting the booming AI infrastructure layer.
opportunities.angle: Threat-actor focused breakdown: what LiteLLM is, how the compromise works, and why AI-adjacent open source is the next big supply-chain target after npm/PyPI.
